text:
A: Hiya. Erm, Lee, is it? I'm Rhys.
B: Yeah. All right.
A: Last one, I think. Or, erm, is it? I've lost track.
B: Think so. Thank god.
A: Ha. Yeah, no, that's fair. Where are you calling from?
B: Wakefield. You're Welsh.
A: Caerphilly, yeah. Just outside Cardiff.
B: Right.
A: Erm... I saw the scarf in your picture. Is that rugby?
B: Trinity. League. You're a union lot down there, aren't you.
A: We are, yeah. I'm not really sporty, to be honest, but I watch the Six Nations with my dad. I get, like, physically tense. Then we lose and he texts me about it for a week. Sort of a post-match report.
B: Martin's union. Told him it's just lads lying in a heap.
A: Ha, I bet he loved that.
B: He took it all right.
A: What do you do, then, for work?
B: Sales rep. Builders' merchants. I'm in the car most of the day. M62.
A: Oh, I'm the same with the A469 into Cardiff. Not the same distance, obviously. It's just a queue for forty minutes.
B: Forty minutes is nowt. Try Junction 26 on a Friday.
A: That's fair, you win. Erm, I'm a video editor. Corporate films, ads, that sort of thing. So I sit in a dark room all day, really. Opposite of you.
B: Saw your photo. Thought you'd be summat like that.
A: Ha. Is that good or bad?
B: Just what I thought. Glasses, poster, bookshelf. Hipster.
A: Yeah, no, that's... that's probably fair. I do have a film camera on the shelf as well, so you've got me bang to rights there. Erm, sorry, what do you do when you're not working?
B: Five-a-side. Rugby. PlayStation with me lad.
A: How old's your lad?
B: Eleven.
A: Oh, nice. Does he play the rugby as well?
B: Nah. FIFA mainly. He's better than me at it, which I don't like.
A: Ha. My wife's a primary teacher, she says they're all experts at the games now, they could probably teach the lessons. Erm, what do you do for tea, when you're on the road all day? I live on meal deals on deadline weeks.
B: Greggs. Or a garage meal deal. Air fryer when I get in.
A: Same. Well, the meal deal bit. And a pint of coffee. Then at the weekend I'll go mad and do a ramen broth for twelve hours, which makes no sense.
B: Twelve hours for some noodles?
A: When you say it like that, yeah.
B: You could get a Pot Noodle.
A: Ha, I could. I'd be lying if I said I hadn't. Erm... sorry, I'm rubbish at the silences.
